## CP-HFP-058 — dst item6 sixteenth step: contract-level finding in the composition binding order (needs a decision)

- Read head_local_runtime.py:223-241 (bind_authority) to settle the fixture shape for the runner tests and instead found a contract-level contradiction in my own frozen composition. bind_authority requires the authority to satisfy generation and session_id equal to the local scope, native_owner equal to the revoker's, and arm_guard and fault_callback EQUAL to the runtime's own bound methods prearm_guard and fault. Those bound methods exist only on the runtime instance, and bound-method equality needs that instance, so a real authority can only be constructed after the runtime exists.
- The composition frozen in CP-HFP-043 cannot satisfy that: bind_native requires the authority before bind_detector, because bind_detector's prerequisite check demands ros and native to be already bound, and bind_runtime comes after inference. The chain is therefore native -> detector -> inference -> runtime, while the runtime demands the authority carry its own arm_guard and fault_callback. No construction order satisfies both, so the runner cannot bind a real authority through the frozen composition at all; the two runner-test failures at HEAD_LOCAL_RUNTIME_PORT_FAULT_OWNER_EXISTS were the first symptom of this, and the earlier HEAD_LOCAL_SCOPE_REUSED and policy-identity failures were separate, now-fixed issues.
- Three candidate resolutions, none of which I may pick unilaterally because they change a frozen E contract: (a) relax the composition's prerequisite chain so native may bind after runtime (the detector check would then require only ros, and the runner's order becomes ros -> detector -> inference -> runtime -> native -> search); (b) let the authority receive arm_guard and fault_callback after construction and re-verify them before bind_native; (c) let the composition accept an authority factory bound to the runtime, called by the runner once the runtime exists. Options (a) and (c) keep bind_authority's strict equality check intact and are the smaller changes; (b) weakens a check that exists to prevent a mismatched authority.
- This is a design question inside my own E implementation, not a deviation from the approved plan, but it changes a frozen contract (CP-HFP-043's binding order and the runner's construction sequence), so per the task rules it goes to the GPT-6.1-Sol High review channel before anything is re-frozen. Nothing was landed this round: the worktree still matches green-028 byte for byte across all 59 curated sources, the runner module is absent, and no gate evidence was added. Retained all, archived NONE, deleted NONE. ExecutionNOT_STARTED, auditNOT_STARTED, qualificationNOT_QUALIFIED; A–G ACTIVE.

## CP-HFP-099 — dst item9: the snapshot_root shape question is settled by evidence

- Attempted the sealed binding-material helper (require_binding_material returning the binding, report and snapshot_root paths) with three cases. The parked schema test fixture (which writes snapshot_root as a ref) and the provider admission check (which currently requires the three names in refs) both have to move with that change.
- The next increment is therefore precise: add the top-level snapshot_root field with directory validation, keep binding and report as refs, update the parked fixture and the provider admission predicate, then land require_binding_material on top of the corrected shape — one RED/GREEN. ## CP-HFP-107 — dst item6: CP-HFP-059 dissolves; the runner needs no external decision

- Re-read the composition's own gate (src/adapters/act/head_execution_composition.py, BIND_ORDER and _require_stage) instead of trusting my earlier reading: _require_stage only refuses a stage whose BIND_ORDER predecessors are not yet BOUND. Constructing an object and binding it are therefore different moments, and the contradiction CP-HFP-059 described came from my assumption that the runtime is constructed and bound in one step.
- The legal order that satisfies every check, with no contract change: bind the stack (ros), construct the local runtime object unbound, construct the authority from that runtime's own prearm_guard and fault (so bind_authority's equality checks pass), bind native, bind the detector built by the owner factory, bind inference, bind the already-constructed runtime, bind the search. Each bind happens after exactly the predecessors the gate demands.
- Consequence recorded, and it retires the blocker: CP-HFP-059 is answered by construction order rather than escalated — the decision request file stays as documentation of a question that turned out not to need an answer, and the parked runner can be landed without any external input. The runner body is now the only remaining E work. Findings in cp-hfp-059-resolution.json (SHA256 prefix f6a72b6ef0cb0536).

## CP-HFP-114 — dst item6: moving native out of the provider pulls the detector with it

- Landed the first half of the CP-HFP-110 move with a valid RED: the provider test's two composition-state assertions were changed to expect ros-only after a detector failure and ros+detector after a clean assemble, and red-071 measured 568 cases, 2 failures, 0 errors, rc 1 — exactly those two assertions, with every other frozen test green. The provider was then changed to stop constructing and binding native and revoker, handing the two constructor entries to the caller instead (RESOURCE_BINDING loses the native/revoker pair, the assemble block stores native_entry/revoker_entry on the handle, and the teardown list drops them).
- green-072 then failed with three EXECUTION_COMPOSITION_REFUSED errors: test_assemble_binds_every_resource_and_returns_the_handle, test_assemble_refuses_a_native_authority_failure_and_tears_down and test_provide_runs_the_plan_runner_and_tears_down_afterwards. The cause is structural and it corrects CP-HFP-110's scope: the composition's gate requires native to be BOUND before detector, so a provider that no longer binds native can no longer bind the detector either. ## CP-HFP-168 — dst item9: safety_inputs is a socket path, so the provider wiring is a real conflict

- Read the authority instead of assuming its input format, and the second missing ref turned out not to be a missing file at all. _MainChannel.__init__(path, *, capability, native_owner, generation, timeout_s, monotonic) takes the filesystem path of a Unix domain socket: it enforces the 107-byte AF_UNIX limit, requires a private parent, lstats the path and connects to it, and validates capability as exactly 32 non-zero bytes with a {uid, pid, start_ticks} owner triple. Nothing reads a document.
- But the provider passes refs['safety_inputs']['path'] as that argument, and the closed schema verifies every ref as a sealed regular file (the same constraint that moved snapshot_root out of refs in CP-HFP-099). So refs['safety_inputs'] can hold neither a socket (the input parser refuses the document) nor a regular file (the authority refuses it): the wiring cannot be satisfied as written. That is also why no safety_inputs file exists anywhere — it was never meant to be one. The decision request now carries this as a contract question with three possible rulings (drop the ref and declare the endpoint at run time, keep a ref as a declaration document the provider resolves, or another ruling), and the finding is item9-safety-inputs-conflict.json, SHA256 prefix 963c55d470b1cea6 (request now SHA256 prefix be6ec72762bd088a).
- This is the kind of question the executor is instructed to escalate rather than settle, so it goes with the local_policy request instead of being patched. Nothing was changed in the worktree (green-103 byte for byte across all 62 curated sources) and no gate passed. Retained all, archived NONE, deleted NONE. ExecutionNOT_STARTED, auditNOT_STARTED, qualificationNOT_QUALIFIED; A–G ACTIVE.

## CP-HFP-169 — dst item9: a fourth, contract-preserving option is offered

- Before anyone reaches for a schema change, there is a fix that adds no field and touches no frozen file, and it follows the pattern the run declarations already set: the endpoint the authority needs is a Unix socket in a private directory under the 107-byte limit, and the run already owns exactly such a directory in its run_root, so the endpoint can be derived as <run_root>/native.sock with the owner triple read from the live process; the capability (32 non-zero bytes shared by the native authority and the revoker) can be generated once per run by the same component that creates the socket, which is also the right place for a per-run secret rather than sealing it in an input document. With that, safety_inputs leaves refs and nothing else moves — the schema keeps its sealed-regular-file rule for the other ten refs, the authority keeps its validated interface, and the document keeps its four declarations plus the snapshot root.

## CP-HFP-405 — dst item9: the case proves the binding-loader seam must stay on the development path
